newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to attract $30 bln FDI by 2000 - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Poland to attract $30 bln FDI by 2000 - finmin.

text.p: Poland is likely to attract nearly $30 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) by the year 2000 as its economy continues to grow, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday.
"So far a dozen or so billion dollars have been invested (since communism fell in 1989) and in 2000 the figure should reach nearly $30 billion," Kolodko told a news conference.
He said that while investors have so far come mainly from Western countries he expected more investment to be brought from the Far East.

"What is significant the investment will be diversified," he said, adding investors will be lured by progressing economic liberalisation and growth, seen sustained at more than five percent until the end of the decade.
Foreign investors so far focused on Poland's car, tobacco, paper, cement and banking sectors.
Analysts say new investors will come to the oil, telecom, energy, insurance and banking sectors, when they open for sale within the next few years.
A recent study by the National Chamber of Commerce showed that foreign investment may reach $21- $22 billion by the year 2000 and is likely to remain a major factor in the country's economic growth.
